attribution_limitations: Source conflict on scan order: the abstract says Ga-68 DOTA-TATE PET/CT was performed and FDG PET/CT was performed on the next day and confirmed the findings, while the case text (FDG PET/CT performed after rising Tg and sternal pain; Ga-68 DOTA-TATE PET/CT "confirmed the findings of FDG PET/CT") and the Figure 2 caption ("confirmed the lesions detected by FDG PET/CT") place FDG PET/CT first. The FDG/Ga-68 relation stays unknown and no fact carries the one-day interval; both versions agree that both scans preceded lu177 DOTA-TATE therapy.
The sentence reporting the first serum Tg and TSH values begins with the male pronoun "His", although the patient is described as a woman with female pronouns elsewhere.

"After 14 months" and "After 6 months" name no anchor event, so the fact times keep a null anchor and these two follow-up results are not ordered against the empirical I-131 dose, the diagnostic scan, each other or the referral; only the "first" serum Tg is ordered before the follow-up Tg. The sentence beginning "According to the guidelines of that time" is incomplete, so the decision it explains is not documented.
It is not stated whether the 200 mci lu177 DOTA-TATE receipt is the first cycle, nor the doses of the cycles; the first and second cycles are mentioned only as anchors for the Tg values.

Dyspnea appears only as a symptom that improved (abstract, discussion); the case text lists sternal pain as the presenting symptom and gives no onset or description of dyspnea. The dyspnea item records only that the symptom existed (implied by its improvement); it is not placed in the post-therapy outcome event and carries no onset time.
The sternal and pulmonary metastases are described from imaging only; no biopsy or histology of the metastases is documented.
